title: Adaptive micro-batch ceilings with QPS smoothing and KV slab allocation
creator: Marcus Li
description:
Problem: Under sustained high QPS spikes we observe sudden GPU memory pressure and tail latency amplification. Continuous batching currently grows micro-batches until a fixed global microbatch_ceiling, which leads to bursty KV cache growth and OOM/eviction storms on multi-tenant GPU pools.

Goal: Implement an adaptive microbatch ceiling and request-level backpressure governor that smooths incoming QPS (short-window EWMA) and enforces a token-budget governor per-stream, combined with a slab allocator for KV-cache entries to reduce fragmentation and make memory usage more predictable. The feature should prevent OOMs, keep 95th percentile latency within SLOs during 99th percentile QPS bursts, and limit eviction churn to <10% of active KV entries per minute.

Constraints: Must be compatible with existing runtime APIs, not add user-visible latency in steady-state, and be deployable incrementally via runtime feature flag and canary pool. Work interacts with batching scheduler, KV cache manager, and GPU memory monitor.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive microbatch ceiling calculation deployed behind feature flag and enabled in canary region
During synthetic QPS spike tests (3x baseline for 10 minutes), 95th token latency increases <20% compared to baseline and 99th token latency <50%
GPU memory headroom maintained: no pool reaches >92% GPU memory utilization during test bursts
KV eviction churn reduced to <10% of active entries/minute compared to current baseline >25%
Automated integration test that simulates mixed short/long context workloads and validates backpressure behaviour added to CI
Telemetry: new dashboard panels for microbatch size distribution, EWMA QPS, token-budget consumption, slab allocator fragmentation metric
tasks: Design adaptive ceiling algorithm: define soft vs hard ceiling, headroom multiplier, burst reservoir and slow-start ramp
Implement short-window EWMA QPS estimator in ingress path and expose to scheduler
Add token-budget governor per request-stream and integrate with scheduler token accounting
Implement KV slab allocator prototype: fixed-size slabs per-model-class and eviction buckets
Instrument GPU memory monitor hooks to trigger proactive backpressure when headroom crosses threshold
Write unit + integration tests for governor and allocator
Create canary rollout plan and prepare dashboards/alerts
Run scale tests and iterate parameters based on results
notes: Design decision: use a 30s EWMA window with alpha=0.2 for smoothing QPS to react to sustained bursts but ignore single-interval jitter
Soft ceiling will allow microbatch growth up to 0.6 * available_tokens_budget, hard ceiling enforces 0.9 * per-GPU token capacity to reserve headroom for KV growth
Burst reservoir: allow temporary overshoot of soft ceiling using a token credit that decays over 60s; prevents immediate backpressure on short bursts

Token-budget governor charges a 'token-cost' per request based on expected output length and model multiplier; requests that exceed current budget are flagged for graceful deferral (429-similar) or routed to lower-cost model variant
KV slab allocator reduces fragmentation by grouping entries by approximate size buckets (small/medium/large); allocator exposes per-slab occupancy and fragmentation ratio metrics
Trade-off: slab approach increases complexity but reduces unpredictable reallocations and OOM triggers; may slightly increase memory overhead (estimated +3-6%)
We considered per-tenant fixed quotas but rejected because it reduces overall throughput and lowers GPU utilization for multi-tenant pools
Interactions with existing KV eviction: keep LRU as secondary policy inside each slab and avoid cross-slab evictions except under emergency compaction
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial design doc posted to Confluence (link in PR #4123). Decided EWMA window and headroom multipliers in design review.
2026-03-04: Prototype of EWMA QPS estimator committed. Scheduler hook added to sample ingress TPS every 250ms.
2026-03-06: Token-budget governor stub implemented; integrates with per-request metadata. Unit tests added for budget accounting.
2026-03-08: KV slab allocator prototyped; microbench shows 18% reduction in allocation variance under synthetic workload.
2026-03-10: First canary deploy to staging pool. Observed reduced eviction churn but slightly higher steady-state memory (~+4%). Tuning underway.
2026-03-12: Load test (3x QPS for 10m) executed. 95th token latency +15%, GPU headroom min 10%, eviction churn 8% — meets acceptance criteria. Preparing rollout notes.
rollout_plan: Step 0: Merge feature-flagged PRs to main behind runtime-1.20 branch
Step 1: Enable in single canary pool (low traffic) for 48h and monitor dashboards/alerts
Step 2: Gradually enable for 10% of pools (diverse instance types) for 72h; adjust reservoir decay and slab sizes if fragmentation >12%
Step 3: Enable for 50% of pools for 48h and validate SLOs and cost impact
Step 4: Full rollout with automated rollback on critical alerts (gpu.pool_memory_headroom_low or eviction churn >20%)
risks: Slab sizing misconfiguration could waste memory or under-allocate for large KV entries; include adaptive slab tuning job
Incorrect token-cost heuristics may penalize legitimate long-output requests; add fallback routing to allow best-effort completion
Cross-component change: scheduler, ingress, KV manager all touch same critical path — require careful staging to avoid regressions
postmortem_plan: If OOM or major SLA breach during rollout: immediate rollback to previous runtime via feature flag
Collect heap dumps and KV slab occupancy traces, run offline allocator simulator to identify mis-sized slabs
Create follow-up ticket with concrete tuning recommendations and update default config
communication: Notify Platform Slack #runtime-ops before canary enable with expected test window
Email on-call 24h prior to 50% rollout and provide rollback playbook
Post short summary to engineering weekly with links to dashboards and PRs after full rollout
